negative_findings.description: No commercial bank in this cell was found to publish a public procurement / tender / 'јавни набавки' page. Navigation extraction of kb.mk showed no procurement section, and no MK-language search surfaced a bank RFP portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero public bank RFP/nabavki pages found across the ten banks in scope.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: MK systemic banks are private and outside the Bureau for Public Procurement regime, so procurement intent is invisible ex ante. Vendor selection can only be reconstructed ex post from press releases, annual reports, app metadata and vendor case studies.

negative_findings.description: https://www.unibank.com.mk/ returned no output on a single WebFetch attempt.
negative_findings.result_summary: One failed fetch; not retried with an alternative client.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: UNIBanka is in the cell scope; the failure is most likely bot defence or a timeout rather than a dead site, so it must be re-attempted with a browser-based fetcher before any conclusion is drawn.

negative_findings.description: The sparkasse.mk homepage fetch exposed no news/press-release link; only a Финансиски извештаи page was located, and that via a site-scoped search rather than on-site navigation.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: An Erste-group bank almost certainly issues press releases; if there is genuinely no on-site archive, coverage of Sparkasse must lean on bankarstvo.mk, LinkedIn and the Erste Group report, which weakens primary-source confidence.

negative_findings.description: Two assumed domains were wrong: ProCredit Bank MK is at pcb.mk (not procreditbank.com.mk) and UNIBanka at unibank.com.mk (not uni.com.mk); kb.com.mk 302-redirects to kb.mk.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a downstream collector from recording live banks as dead sources on bad seed URLs.

negative_findings.description: Across the Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB and Halkbank digital-launch announcements surfaced in this pass, no supplier/system vendor was named in the bank's own text (the sole partner named anywhere was KIBS, the domestic digital-certificate issuer, in a Stopanska banka item).
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank press releases describe capability, not supplier.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Establishes that the direct sources alone cannot answer 'who supplied this' — vendor-side collateral and technical fingerprints (app package ids, API portals, job ads) are structurally necessary, not optional supplements.

negative_findings.description: Halkbank MK, ProCredit (pcb.mk) and UNIBanka news/annual-report index paths were not individually confirmed by fetch within this pass; only their root domains and product pages were established.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three of ten banks have unconfirmed newsroom/report paths.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are hypotheses for the next pass, not verified sources; recording them as confirmed would overstate coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Halkbank, ProCredit, UNIBanka and Centralna kooperativna banka are covered only at root-domain or reports-page level; their press-release archives are not yet located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted per-bank crawl (sitemap.xml, /novosti, /soopstenija, /za-nas, .nspx enumeration) with a browser-capable fetcher to pin the news index for each.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank IT job advertisements — which name concrete platforms (core, card management, AML, ESB) — were not searched at all this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search vrabotuvanje.com.mk, pazar3.mk/vrabotuvanje, mojaplata.mk and bank career pages for MK bank IT roles; extract named technologies as installed-base evidence.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one vendor mirror (Asseco SEE) was explored. Other likely suppliers to MK banks (card personalisation, ATM/POS, digital onboarding, PKI) have their own case-study libraries that were not searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Once each bank's stack is hypothesised, run the same vendor-side reverse search per supplier candidate and per press-release-partner name.

coverage_gaps.description: No historical back-fill depth was assessed beyond noting NLB's 2016-2026 year filters; the archive depth of Komercijalna, Stopanska and the smaller banks is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe each newsroom's oldest reachable item and record archive depth per bank so trend analysis is not built on uneven history.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language subsidiary reporting by foreign parents (NLB Group, Erste/Steiermärkische, ProCredit Holding, Halkbank TR, CCB Sofia, OTP for Stopanska) was not systematically collected; group reports often describe MK-subsidiary IT programmes in more detail than the local site.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the parent groups' investor-relations report libraries as an en-language layer and grep for Macedonia/Skopje/subsidiary mentions.

coverage_gaps.description: SEINet's technical access characteristics (JS gating, session requirements, bulk export) were not tested, despite it being the single highest-leverage pointer in the cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do a dedicated access-feasibility spike on seinet.com.mk with a headless browser and document a repeatable extraction path per issuer.

brief: MK commercial banks form a two-layer source landscape: each bank's own Macedonian-language newsroom and annual-report section (NLB's year-filtered 2016-2026 press archive and Stopanska's /novosti feed are the richest; Komercijalna, Sparkasse, TTK and CKB expose reports reliably but news less so), sitting above SEINet/Macedonian Stock Exchange as a single regulated pointer into every listed bank's price-sensitive filings. Critically, no bank in this cell publishes a procurement or tender page — procurement is private, confirming the cell rationale — and the bank releases found here describe new capability without ever naming the supplier (the lone exception being KIBS in a Stopanska item). Vendor identity therefore has to be recovered indirectly: vendor-side collateral (Asseco SEE hosts a named Komercijalna banka case study and MK delivery news), mobile-app package fingerprints (NLB mKlik ships under an Asseco 'jimba' Android namespace), open-banking/API registries, and trade media bankarstvo.mk and it.mk which reprint releases the banks do not archive. Next-pass priorities are pinning the newsroom paths for Halkbank, ProCredit, UNIBanka and CKB, testing SEINet's extractability, and mining MK bank IT job ads for installed-platform names.
